Metadata.title: Rehla — Your companion on the road to the light
Metadata.description: An AI-powered platform that accompanies new Muslims from the moment they declare the Shahada to confident practice and belonging, in their own language and grounded in approved sources.

Home.eyebrow: For new Muslims, after the Shahada
Home.title: Rehla
Home.tagline: Your companion on the road to the light
Home.intro: Rehla is an AI-powered platform that accompanies new Muslims from the moment they declare the Shahada to confident practice and belonging, in their own language and grounded in approved sources.

why.title: Why Rehla
why.body: Right after the Shahada, a new Muslim faces practical questions that cannot wait: how to purify and pray, how to behave in a mosque for the first time, what the Arabic texts around them mean, and who to turn to when stuck. Human follow-up alone cannot be present in their every day.

closing.title: The road is ahead of you
closing.body: Start at the first station, at your own pace.

Home.askSpecialistLine: A question that troubles you, or need a trusted body to ask? These licensed organisations in Saudi Arabia can answer.

learn.title: Steps
learn.line: Short lessons along a road of three stations, starting wherever you choose.

practice.line: Try what you learned with your own hands, and gather provisions for the road.

rafiq.title: Ask Rafiq
rafiq.line: Ask about your lesson or a word you did not understand; he shows the source of every answer.

specialists.title: Specialists
specialists.line: Licensed organisations that answer when your question needs a specialist.

trust.title: How we keep it trustworthy
trust.verbatim: Text from approved sources, shown word for word

AiNotice.label: About Rafiq
AiNotice.title: Rafiq is an AI tool.
AiNotice.body: It is not a human scholar. It answers from approved sources and cites them, and it does not issue fatwas. For personal matters, consult a qualified scholar.

Rafiq.title: Ask Rafiq
Rafiq.description: Ask about what you are learning. Rafiq answers from approved sources and shows you where each answer comes from.
Rafiq.emptyTitle: Rafiq is ready to walk with you
Rafiq.emptyBody: Ask a question about Islam or about one of your lessons. If Rafiq finds no reliable source, he will say so and point you to a specialist.

starters.prayers: How many prayers are there in a day?

Rafiq.enterHint: Press Enter to ask, Shift+Enter for a new line.
Rafiq.thinking: Rafiq is looking in the sources…
Rafiq.disclosure: Rafiq is an AI tool, not a scholar. Check what he says against his sources.
Rafiq.laterTitle: This comes later on your road
Rafiq.laterBody: It is covered in the lesson “<lesson></lesson>”.
Rafiq.smalltalk: Rafiq is with you on the road. Ask him about a lesson, a word you came across, or how to do an act of worship.

errors.rateLimited: You have asked several questions in a short time. Wait a minute, then ask again.
errors.unavailable: Rafiq cannot be reached right now. Try again in a little while, or talk to a specialist.
errors.error: Something went wrong while asking Rafiq. Please try again.

fatwa.title: This needs a scholar
fatwa.body: You are asking for a religious ruling (a fatwa). Rafiq does not give rulings; a qualified scholar who knows the details should answer you.

personalCase.title: This needs a specialist
personalCase.body: This is about your own situation. Rafiq can share general information only; a specialist can listen to you and advise you.

disputed.title: This needs a specialist
disputed.body: Scholars differ on matters like this, and Rafiq will not settle it on his own. A qualified specialist can explain it to you.

noSource.title: No reliable source found
noSource.body: Rafiq did not find a reliable source for this, so he will not guess. A specialist can help you.

noEvidence.title: No matching evidence
noEvidence.body: No evidence matching this was found in the approved sources, and Rafiq will not make one up.

verification.title: Rafiq could not check his answer
verification.body: Rafiq could not match his answer to its sources, so he will not show it. Try other words, or ask a specialist.

offTopic.title: Outside Rafiq's road
offTopic.body: Rafiq answers questions about Islam and about your lessons. This question is outside that.

distress.title: You do not have to carry this alone
distress.body: What you are going through deserves care from people who can listen. These specialists can help.

danger.title: Please get help now
danger.body: If you or someone else is in danger, contact your local emergency services now, or a person you trust. You can also reach these specialists.

Specialist.title: Talk to a specialist
Specialist.description: Licensed bodies you can turn to with your own questions.
Specialist.why: Rafiq is an AI tool. It explains what the lessons say, but it does not give rulings on anyone's personal situation. For your own case, speak with a specialist.
Specialist.nationalNote: National channel, available inside Saudi Arabia
Specialist.cityHelp: Choose your city to see associations near you. Your choice stays on this device.
Specialist.outside: If you are outside Saudi Arabia, ask the nearest trusted Islamic centre in your country.
Specialist.privacy: Rehla shares nothing about you with these bodies. Whether and how you contact them is entirely your choice.

lines.lantern: I'm Rafiq, a small lantern walking with you on the road to the light.
lines.light: The light I carry is not knowledge of my own: when you ask, I look in approved sources and show you where each answer comes from.
lines.limits: I am not a scholar and I do not give rulings. When your question needs a specialist, I will say so and point you to one.
lines.ask: Ask me about your lesson, a word you did not understand, or how to do an act of worship. No question is too small; lanterns do not get tired.

chips.specialist: Refers you to a specialist when needed

Guide.label: How Rehla works

road.title: Your road, step by step
road.body: Three stations: the beginning, then purification, then prayer. You choose where to start and continue whenever you like.

class.title: Every lesson is a small class
class.body: A board where the lesson is written line by line, with Rafiq beside you. The text comes from approved sources, and its source is written under it.

hands.title: You learn with your hands
hands.body: You put the steps of wudu in order, build a rak'ah, and move the sun to find each prayer's time. Then short questions fix what you learned, and a stamp in your journal for every lesson you finish.

question.title: Try a question
question.body: This is how the short questions come after a lesson. Answer it; a mistake does not count against you, and every lesson you finish is stamped in your journal.

together.title: You are not alone
together.body: Ask Rafiq whenever you need something explained, and when your question needs a specialist we point you to one.
